title: The Issues Practice in Context

header.html: Apply the issues practice: issue management approach, issue register, issue report; areas of focus of key roles; issue types, handling steps, change authority, change budget and escalation; analyze whether an issues approach is effective and fit for purpose considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Areas of focus of the key roles

html:
1Purpose, objectives and principles

The issues practice captures, assesses and resolves issues so the project stays in control and the baseline is changed only on purpose. An issue is something that has happened, was not planned and needs management action. The baseline is the approved version of the products and plans. All changes start as issues, but not every issue is a change.

It serves manage by exception (decisions at the right level within tolerances), continued business justification (every decision is judged for its effect on the case), focus on products (baselined products are protected), define roles (who decides what) and manage by stages.

Exam tip

. Has happened is an issue; might happen is a risk. A request for a new feature is already an issue, because the request has been made.

2The key management products

Product What it is for
Issue management approach How issues and changes are handled: steps, roles, how issues are rated, change control and delegated authority. Part of the initiation documentation
Issue register A record of all issues, their type, status and the decisions made. Part of the project log
Issue report A detailed description of one issue, with its impact analysis and a recommendation

Issue types: a request for change (a proposal to alter a baseline), an off-specification (something that is, or will be, missing from what was agreed) and a problem or concern (anything else needing management action). The book also treats a business opportunity as a possible source of issues. Check the book for the exact list.

Exam tip

. New wish is a request for change; failing the agreed specification is an off-specification. The type decides the route: a request for change goes through change control.

3Areas of focus of the key roles

Role Focus in the issues practice
Executive Decides escalated issues; the business case is protected
Senior user Judges the user impact of changes and off-specifications
Senior supplier Judges the impact on the supplier's work and cost
Project manager Makes sure issues are captured, assessed and managed; escalates when tolerance is threatened
Team manager Raises issues found in the work packages
Change authority Approves or rejects changes within the authority delegated by the board
Project assurance Checks the issue procedure is followed
Project support Keeps the issue register and records of baselined products

The change budget is a sum the board sets aside to pay for approved changes. The change authority decides within its delegation and the change budget. Check the book's table for exact responsibilities.

4Effective management and techniques

Step What happens
Capture Record the issue in the issue register; decide its type; small issues can be dealt with quickly but are still recorded
Assess Analyze impact on cost, time, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability; consider urgency
Propose Set out options and a recommendation, in an issue report when it is significant
Decide The person or group with authority decides, or escalates
Implement Carry it out; update plans, registers and baselines; tell those affected

The book may word some steps differently; the order and purpose are what matter.

Escalation by tolerance. The project manager decides what can be resolved within the stage tolerance. The change authority decides changes within its delegated limits and the change budget. If a decision would push the stage beyond tolerance, the project manager raises an exception report and the board decides. If project tolerance is threatened, the board goes to the corporate level.

Exam tip

. Check the tolerance, then the delegation. Inside tolerance and delegation the project manager or change authority decides; outside, escalate. A board decision on every small issue is a red flag, and so is a quiet decision beyond tolerance.

5Judging a scenario

An effective approach Red flags (not fit for purpose)
Every issue is captured and assessed for impact Issues agreed in corridors or by email and never recorded
Baselined products change only through formal change control Informal scope creep: a user asks the team and the team just does it
Decided by the right level (project manager, change authority, board) Project manager approves a change beyond tolerance, or the board decides trivial items
Change authority acts within delegated limits and the change budget Changes approved after the change budget is spent, with no escalation
Impact on the business case and on benefits considered Cost of a change judged but its effect on benefits ignored
Registers, plans and baselines updated after the decision Decision made, but the plan and product register stay unchanged
Lessons recorded from repeat issues The same off-specification repeats

Tailoring.

Context How issue management changes
Small internal project One person as change authority; a simple register; the same steps
Agile or hybrid delivery Reordering the backlog inside the baseline and tolerances is routine change control; changes beyond them are formal
Large or multi-party project Several change authorities; supplier contract variations follow change control
Sustainability or data concerns Every change is assessed for sustainability and data effects
Exam tip

. Agile does not remove change control; it moves the line. Backlog reprioritization within the baseline and tolerances is routine; a change to the baseline or beyond tolerance still goes through formal control.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A harbor pilot asks Wei Chen to add a seasonal permit type to the build. Wei agrees because the work is small and starts it without telling Sam Okafor. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because small additions let the team show flexibility to the users it serves daily
  • BYes, because a team manager may approve any change that fits the work package tolerance
  • CNo, because it is a proposed change to the baseline and must go through change control
  • DNo, because a team manager must send every user request straight to the Executive
Show the answer

Answer: C. Work package tolerance does not give authority over scope, so the request must be captured and decided at the right level instead of informal scope creep.

S2A request for change costing 6,000 is within the 24,000 change budget and within the authority the board delegated to Tomas Reyes. Who should decide it?

  • ASam Okafor, the project manager
  • BTomas Reyes, change authority
  • CWei Chen, the team manager
  • DMarta Quinn, the Executive
Show the answer

Answer: B. The change authority decides changes within the delegation and change budget, which keeps the board free for exceptions.

S3A request for change on Project Harbor would cost 40,000, beyond the 24,000 change budget and the stage tolerance. What should Sam Okafor do?

  • AAsk Tomas Reyes to approve it and tell Wei Chen to start the work
  • BReject the request quietly without a record to protect the change budget
  • CApprove it himself and mention the decision in the next highlight report
  • DEscalate it to the board with an issue report and a recommendation
Show the answer

Answer: D. The change exceeds both the delegation and the tolerance, so manage by exception requires the board to decide on a recommendation.

S4Sam Okafor needs a detailed write-up of one off-specification found in testing, with its impact analysis and a recommendation for the board. Which management product is it?

  • AIssue register
  • BException report
  • CLessons report
  • DIssue report
Show the answer

Answer: D. The issue report describes one issue in detail with analysis and recommendation; the register lists all issues and the exception report is for a forecast tolerance breach.

S5Sam Okafor records a testing defect in the issue register as an off-specification, assesses its impact, and decides to rework it within the stage tolerance. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because an issue resolved within tolerance may be decided by the project manager once recorded
  • BYes, because an off-specification is a team matter and needs no entry in the issue register
  • CNo, because every off-specification must be approved by the project board before rework starts
  • DNo, because the project manager may never decide an issue and must send each to the change authority
Show the answer

Answer: A. Within tolerance the project manager decides, provided the issue is captured and assessed, as manage by exception intends.

S6Wei Chen's agile team reorders backlog items each sprint within the baselined acceptance criteria and stage tolerances. Sam Okafor wonders whether every reorder needs a formal request for change. What should he do?

  • ARequire an issue report and board approval for every single reorder of the backlog
  • BBan all backlog changes during the stage so that the baseline stays protected throughout
  • CAllow any backlog change at all, because agile teams are expected to manage themselves
  • DMake reorders within baseline and tolerances routine and send the rest through change control
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tailoring moves where the formal line sits for agile delivery but does not remove change control of the baseline or tolerances.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is an issue?

Show the answer

An event that has happened, was not planned and needs management action.

R2Name the three issue types.

Show the answer

Request for change, off-specification, and problem or concern.

R3What is the change budget?

Show the answer

Money the board sets aside to pay for approved changes.

R4Who decides changes within delegated limits?

Show the answer

The change authority.

R5What is a baseline?

Show the answer

The approved version of the products and plans used as the reference for control.

R6When does an issue go to the board?

Show the answer

When resolving it would exceed the project manager's tolerance or the change authority's delegation.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Issue has happened, unplanned, needs management action
Types request for change, off-specification, problem or concern
Steps capture, assess, propose, decide, implement
Change authority decides changes within delegated limits
Change budget set aside by the board for approved changes
Issue report one issue in detail with analysis and recommendation
Escalation by tolerance: project manager, change authority, board, corporate
Tailoring agile moves the line; change control of the baseline stays
